title: Private VPC Discovery - Granite Bank
summary: Initial discovery focused on network design for private VPC deployment, region/data residency constraints, authentication/KMS requirements, and open questions around peering vs PrivateLink. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Private with a pilot target in Q2.
topics: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink, private endpoints, region constraints (us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 replication), routing/Transit Gateway, KMS/HSM + key policies, SOC2/SAML requirements, latency vs egress cost tradeoffs, demo/benchmark next steps
action_items: Samira: Send SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and Redwood Private network architecture doc - due 2027-03-18
Dante: Prepare sample Terraform + network diagram for Granite Bank's VPC setup (transit gateway + endpoints) - due 2027-03-19
Liam: Share current VPC CIDR blocks and peering restrictions, plus any transit gateway IDs we need for testing - due 2027-03-18
Priya: Provide list of required compliance artifacts and KMS key policies to validate for PoC - due 2027-03-20
next_steps: Schedule SE deep dive / network planning session (1 hour)
Provision trial Private tenant in us-east-1 for pilot
Share pricing estimate for Dedicated vs Private (incl. egress/peering costs)
Run a small latency/cost benchmark with their sample prompt set
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Dante (Redwood SE), Maya (Granite VP Eng), Liam (Cloud Architect), Priya (Security)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood Inference, AE working with finance verticals. Quick intro then we'll hand to Dante for the technical overview.
[00:18] Maya: Thanks Samira, hi team, Maya here, we'll probably have a lot of network questions, Liam and Priya are on to help.
[00:24] Dante: Hi all, Dante, Solutions Eng. Today we'll focus on Private / VPC deployments - how Redwood can run in your VPC, options for connectivity, and what we need for a pilot.
[00:36] Liam: Quick context - Granite Bank has an existing AWS footprint, primary region us-east-1, some DR in eu-west-1. We need data to stay in those regions; we can't send traffic to public endpoints outside those regions.
[00:48] Priya: And from security we need KMS-managed keys, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SAML SSO, RBAC, and proof of SOC 2.
[00:59] Samira: Absolutely, those are standard asks. For Private we support customer-managed VPC with either VPC peering or PrivateLink style private endpoints depending on topology.
[01:15] Maya: Can you explain differences? We've heard peering can be 1:1 and gets messy; PrivateLink sounds cleaner but costy.
[01:23] Dante: Yeah good question. High level: VPC peering is a direct route between two VPCs. It's simple but if you have many accounts, peering mesh becomes a pain. Transit Gateway helps centralize routing. PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) gives you interface endpoints backed by ENIs managed by Redwood in our VPC; your traffic stays private and hits a network interface. PrivateLink avoids exposing service IPs and typically simplifies cross-account access.
[01:46] Liam: Are you saying Redwood will create endpoints in our account or we create an endpoint to your service?
[01:52] Dante: Typically you create an interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce...) in your VPC that connects to our service. We can provide a service name. Alternatively, if you prefer, we can peer our service VPC with yours or connect via Transit Gateway. For larger setups transit-gw peering + route propagation is common.
[02:10] Priya: What about egress / NAT? We need to avoid public egress.
[02:15] Dante: For Private deployment in a VPC, the inference nodes have private ENIs only. Outbound to internet isn't required; we support access to S3 via VPC endpoints, and if your environment blocks egress entirely, we can arrange a customer-managed NAT or VPC endpoint for necessary telemetry buckets.
[02:31] Maya: Do we need to open ports? Security groups?
[02:35] Dante: We'll provide the minimal security group rules. Usually we need TCP 443 outbound to the PrivateLink service or allow our peering CIDRs. We also support mTLS for control plane connections if you want mutual TLS.
[02:50] Liam: Region question: our EU customers must have data in eu-west-1. Can Redwood run Private in both regions and replicate models?
[02:58] Samira: Yes, we can provision Private deployments per region. For replicate/active-active you can choose model sync and data residency policies; many customers run a primary in us-east-1 and a secondary in eu-west-1. Pricing and capacity are region-specific.
[03:14] Liam: How about latency? If we peer to your service in us-east-1 but our users are in eu-west-1, that's bad.
[03:20] Dante: Correct—latency matters. We'll recommend colocating inference in the region nearest your traffic. For multi-region traffic you can use smart routing/policy to direct EU calls to eu-west-1.
[03:30] Priya: KMS integration: do you support customer-managed KMS keys (CMKs) and HSM-backed keys?
[03:36] Dante: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. For Private we can use your KMS keys for model artifacts and any customer data stored in the Private control plane. If you require HSM-backed keys, we can discuss an HSM integration pattern or on-prem HSM options for high-compliance customers.
[03:52] Maya: Audit logs and SIEM forwarding?
[03:55] Dante: We can stream audit logs to your S3 bucket or push via an HTTPS endpoint. Many customers forward CloudTrail-style logs and application-level audit events to their SIEM. We'll include log formats in the security docs.
[04:08] Maya: Ok. What about model updates and rollouts—how are those handled in Private?
[04:13] Samira: The Console supports pinned model versions, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. For Private we replicate the control plane into your environment; rollouts are orchestrated via the same APIs. Dante: For strict isolation you can control update windows and approve model versions.
[04:31] Liam: Network constraints: our VPCs use /16s reserved for internal infra. Any hard requirements on CIDR sizes?
[04:38] Dante: We ask for a /24 for the interface endpoint ENIs or a range of peering CIDRs depending on topology. We'll include exact requirements in the Terraform sample. Transit Gateway attachments need standard route propagation.
[04:48] Priya: If we use PrivateLink, what's the bandwidth and cost profile? We're concerned about per-GB charges.
[04:55] Dante: PrivateLink incurs per-GB data processing and endpoint hour charges from AWS, plus our egress pricing if applicable. Peering + TGW has different egress math—sometimes cheaper at scale but more operational overhead. We'll model both scenarios for your expected token throughput.
[05:12] Maya: For POC we just need a small pilot for 2-3 models and up to 50 RPS. How quickly can we stand that up?
[05:20] Samira: Pilot timeline depends on network readiness. If we get your CIDR blocks and a VPC endpoint created we can provision within 1-2 weeks. If you require peering + TGW it might be 2-3 weeks for network approvals.
[05:31] Liam: For the endpoint creation who does the work? We need IaC (Terraform).
[05:35] Dante: We will provide sample Terraform and CloudFormation templates. We don't deploy into your account; your infra team applies the templates. During the SE deep dive we'll walk through the apply.
[05:47] Liam: Any special IAM roles?
[05:50] Dante: Minimal cross-account roles if you want automated S3 access. Otherwise, we ask for a service account with restricted permissions for storage and logs. We'll share least-privilege policy.
[06:01] Priya: Encryption in transit — do you support TLS 1.2+? mTLS?
[06:04] Dante: Yes TLS 1.2/1.3 and we support optional mTLS. We also support SAML SSO for user access to Console and SCIM for provisioning.
[06:15] Maya: Can we have an on-prem option? Some of our systems are air-gapped.
[06:19] Samira: We have an on-prem package for fully isolated deployments but that requires a project engagement. For the initial pilot Private VPC is usually sufficient. On-prem is possible but will add time/cost.
[06:32] Maya: Who owns monitoring? We want observability into token costs per customer and latencies.
[06:37] Dante: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. For Private we can integrate with your Datadog/CloudWatch and forward metrics.
[06:49] Priya: Regulatory: do you have a SOC2 report and ISO stuff?
[06:52] Samira: Yes we will share SOC2 Type II and our security whitepaper. Those are in the docs I'll send.
[06:58] Liam: If we go for Dedicated vs Private what's the difference network-wise?
[07:03] Dante: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood-managed infra but still in our cloud tenancy—network access is via secure endpoints. Private gives you a deployment that sits in your VPC with customer-managed networking. Dedicated is easier to start; Private gives maximum isolation and control.
[07:18] Maya: Cost tradeoffs?
[07:20] Samira: Dedicated tends to be lower operational setup but has different pricing—Reserved capacity vs Private which is more project-based and includes network design. We'll put numbers in the proposal based on your RPS and token volumes.
[07:32] Liam: Any gotchas around cross-account VPC peering and Transit Gateway attachments—like blackhole routes?
[07:38] Dante: You'll want to ensure route propagation and avoid overlapping CIDRs. Transit Gateway is recommended when you scale to many VPCs. We'll include a route diagram showing recommended BGP-less TGW route tables.
[07:50] Maya: Can we test with synthetic traffic first?
[07:53] Dante: Yes we'll run a benchmark with your prompt set. For latency/cost analysis we prefer you provide a sample workload—token distribution and request per minute.
[08:02] Priya: Are there any third-party dependencies that would send PII out?
[08:06] Dante: For Private deployments we avoid third-party telemetry. Any integrations are opt-in and we can disable outbound telemetry entirely, or push logs to your S3/SIEM.
[08:15] Samira: Quick recap and next steps?
[08:18] Liam: We'll send CIDR blocks and any TGW constraints.
[08:21] Priya: I'll list required compliance artifacts and whether we need HSM.
[08:24] Maya: We'll book the SE deep dive next week.
[08:28] Samira: Great. We'll follow up with the SOC2, network requirements doc, Terraform sample, and a pricing estimate.
[08:33] Maya: One last question—how do you handle failover if a region goes down?
[08:38] Dante: We support automatic fallback policies. For Private we'd recommend a warm standby in the secondary region and route changes via your DNS or load balancer; we can help design failover runbooks.
[08:49] Samira: Thanks everyone, we'll send the materials and set up the deep dive.
[08:52] End of recording (roughly 52 minutes). Note: transcription contains occasional word swaps and punctuation artifacts due to auto-transcribe.
